item.title: Inprint Andrea Bajani & Claire Vaye Watkins Reading
item.description:
Monday, August 24, 2026 at 7:30 PM

Location: Congregation Emanu El, 1500 Sunset Boulevard, Houston, TX, 77005

Season tickets are on sale here.   Andrea Bajani and Claire Vaye Watkins will read from their new novels The Anniversary (translated by Geoffrey Brock) and Yellow Pine, respectively, followed by an on-stage conversation led by professor and National Book Critics Circle Award finalist Lacy M. Johnson. The evening will conclude with a book sale and signing. The event is presented as part of the 2026/2027 Inprint Margarett Root Brown Reading Series.  Andrea Bajani is one of the most recognized and lauded authors of contemporary Italian and European literature. His many novels include If You Kept a Record of Sins, called “astonishing” by The New York Times, and Every Promise, which won the Bagutta Prize, the oldest Italian literary prize. A self-described existential writer, he often examines the personal, philosophical, and political, while confronting the unanswerable. A professor and international writer-in-residence at Rice University, Bajani joins us with his latest novel, The Anniversary, which won the 2025 Strega Prize, one of Europe’s major literary awards. Currently being translated into more than 25 languages, The Anniversary is a subtle yet heartrending portrait of an abusive marriage in patriarchal Italy and a son’s liberating decision to cut contact with his parents. The Times Literary Supplement writes, “Bajani’s prose is sharp and brims with psychological insights . . . Perhaps its most salient feature—in deft translation by Geoffrey Brock—is its skill at depicting alienation . . . Like Albert Camus, Bajani is a poet of estrangement.” Claire Vaye Watkins has been called “the most riveting voice of the unsalvageable West” (Los Angeles Times). Her debut novel Gold Fame Citrus, inspired by the Californian drought and by the lives of outcasts in the desert, blends climate fiction with environmental history. Born in Bishop, California and raised in the Mojave Desert on the Amargosa River, Watkins is also the author of the novel I Love You But I’ve Chosen Darkness and the short story collection Battleborn, winner of the Story Prize, the Dylan Thomas Prize, and the New York Public Library’s Young Lions Fiction Award. A National Book Foundation “5 Under 35” honoree and a Guggenheim Fellow, Watkins comes to Houston with her newest work Yellow Pine, described by author Megha Majumdar as “an exhilarating novel about a woman in the Mojave desert who wants to be a mother one more time, wants to love freely and arrange her life freely, wants to live outside the maze of money and ads and being sold to, a novel with huge and electric convictions.” Lacy M. Johnson is a Houston-based professor, curator, and activist, and is author of The Reckonings and The Other Side — both National Book Critics Circle Award finalists — and Trespasses. She is editor, with the designer Cheryl Beckett, of More City Than Water: A Houston Flood Atlas. She teaches creative nonfiction at Rice University, where she is the Director of the MFA in Creative Writing Program, and is also the Founding Director of the Houston Flood Museum.

item.title: First Fridays Presents John Milkereit
item.description:
Friday, September 4, 2026 at 7:30 PM

Location: Inprint House, 1520 W Main St, Houston, TX, 77006, United States

Free and open to the public Doors @ 7 pm Reading @ 7:30 pm Followed by an Open mic Inprint is proud to serve as the host for the First Fridays Reading Series. The First Fridays Reading Series is the oldest poetry series in Houston and was organized by Robert Clark from 1975-2019. Today, First Fridays events are curated and hosted by local community members. The September featured reader will be John Milkereit. John lives in Houston, Texas working as a mechanical engineer. His poetry journey did not begin well after being forced to read “Beowulf” in 6th grade. Several decades later, he found himself enjoying a poetry seminar at his local church on the poetry of Billy Collins, and then he took his first poetry class at Inprint in 2005. Later, he went on to complete an MFA in Creative Writing at the Rainier Writing Workshop. His poems have since appeared in various literary journals such as The Comstock Review, San Pedro River Review, and Naugatuck River Review. In December, Kelsay Books released his fifth collection of poems entitled, The Beginning of Undoing. For more information about the First Fridays Reading Series, click here. To join the First Fridays Facebook group, click here.

item.title: Inprint Cool Brains! Series presents Rex Ogle
item.description:
Sunday, September 13, 2026 at 3 PM

Location: Meyerland Performing and Visual Arts Middle School, 10410 Manhattan Drive, Houston, TX, 77096, United States

Free and open to the public Free copies of one of Rex Ogle’s newest books for the first 100 families Presentation and Q&A by the author Meet the author followed by a book sale and signing Bus scholarships available for student groups – full scholarships for public schools, partial scholarships for private schools upon availability. For information, email info@inprint.org Discounted books available through Brazos Bookstore And more! The 2026/2027 Inprint Cool Brains! Series proudly presents award-winning author Rex Ogle, sharing his new books Fruitcake, a graphic novel about surviving middle school and finding the courage to be yourself, and Absent, a middle grade novel about three boys who skip school, told in verse, prose, and comics. Rex Ogle is the author of more than 100 books for kids, including comics, graphic novels, and memoirs—most notably Free Lunch (winner of the ALA/YALSA award for Excellence in Nonfiction), Abuela Don’t Forget Me (ALA/YALSA award for Excellence in Nonfiction finalist), Road Home (a Micheal Printz Honor and Stonewall Honor book), and middle grade graphic novels Four Eyes and Pizza Face. Under his pseudonym Rey Terciero, he has also reimagined classics as modern and diverse graphic novels, including Meg, Jo, Beth, & Amy, Northranger (nominated for both Harvey and GLAAD Media Awards), and Dan in Green Gables (nominated for a GLAAD Media Award). Born and raised in Texas, Rex now lives in Los Angeles where he writes every day—when he’s not reading X-Men, gaming with friends, or chasing his dog, Toby, trying to score a hug. Described as “funny, sad, goofy and poignant; a winner” (Kirkus starred review), Fruitcake is the third and final installment of Ogle’s highly popular Four Eyes graphic novel series, which tackles relatable middle school themes like bullying, puberty, building self-confidence, and navigating friendships. Eighth grade isn’t off to a great start for Rex. Everyone seems to be coupling up, and he’s starting to feel like an outsider—until he meets Charlotte. She’s fearless, smart, pretty, and, best of all, she likes him back. But as wonderful as Charlotte is, Rex can’t stop thinking about someone else: Drew, Rex’s childhood best friend. Suddenly, Rex is navigating feelings he never expected. With strong opinions swirling at home and church, Rex begins to question his own worth and what his feelings truly mean. Featuring Dave Valeza’s vibrant, colorful, and engaging illustrations, Fruitcake is a heartfelt story of laughter and fear, crushes and coming out, and the courage it takes to embrace who you are. With illustrations by LJ-Baptiste, Absent explores school absenteeism in a compelling, entertaining, and utterly distinct middle grade novel. With a dad in jail and a lack of teachers interested in helping him learn, Manny doesn’t see the point in anything besides skateboarding and writing lyrics. Calvin has so many responsibilities to his father and little brothers that when his bike is stolen, he can’t make it to school on time. And while Liam is studious and wants to become a doctor, he is tormented by bullies and hides out in an unused janitor’s closet instead of going to class. When the boys are thrown together in detention, they realize that they might still have a lot to learn—not just from their teachers, but from each other. Absent tells the boys’ stories in three distinct voices: Manny’s in verse, Calvin’s as a comic, and Liam’s as a prose journal. ***Please note that the book signing will be conducted on a first-come, first-served basis. Upon entering the theater, people wishing to have books signed will be given a number, and the book signing will take place in numerical order after the on-stage presentation.***

item.title: Inprint Claudia Rankine Reading
item.description:
Monday, September 14, 2026 at 7:30 PM

Location: Brockman Hall for Opera, Rice University, Entrance #18 off Rice Boulevard, Houston, TX, 77005

General admission tickets will go on sale on Tuesday, August 25, 2026 at 12 pm. Season tickets are on sale here. Claudia Rankine will read from her new hybrid-genre work Triage, followed by an on-stage conversation led by poet and Rice University professor Phillip B. Williams. The evening will conclude with a book sale and signing. The event is presented as part of the 2026/2027 Inprint Margarett Root Brown Reading Series.  Whether writing about intimacy or alienation, Claudia Rankine possesses a voice of unrelenting candor that “shimmers with wisdom and fury” (The Telegraph). A MacArthur Fellow, Rankine is the author of five collections of poetry, including her bestselling Citizen: An American Lyric, which explores what it means to be an American citizen in a “post-racial” society. A defining text for our time, Citizen won the National Book Critics Circle Award, the NAACP Image Award, the PEN Open Book Award, and the Los Angeles Times Book Prize. She is also the author of three plays, including Provenance of Beauty: A South Bronx Travelogue, which is performed on a bus ride through the Bronx; and is the editor of several anthologies, including The Racial Imaginary: Writers on Race in the Life of the Mind. Rankine returns to Inprint with her genre-defying new work Triage, which collides the lyric with narrative, memoir, image, and essay to offer her most personal and emotionally resonant writing yet. Triage follows the turbulent friendship between two characters, the narrator and the theorist, self-identified sisters struggling to define their wounded histories and their shared but separate lives. According to Jamaica Kincaid, “Claudia Rankine’s remarkable, outstanding odyssey—an account of our present, which is also our past, which is always our future—is beautifully rendered in a kaleidoscope of images and sensations. . . . Triage is exquisite.”

item.description:
Monday, October 5, 2026 at 7:30 PM

Location: Alley Theatre, 615 Texas Avenue, Houston, TX, 77002

General admission tickets will go on sale on Tuesday, September 15, 2026 at 12 pm. Season tickets are on sale here. Ayad Akhtar will read from his new novel The Radiance, followed by an on-stage conversation led by a local author/journalist. The evening will conclude with a book sale and signing. The event is presented as part of the 2026/2027 Inprint Margarett Root Brown Reading Series.  Pulitzer Prize winner Ayad Akhtar’s new novel The Radiance is “simply put, a work of genius. Through unforgettable characters Akhtar explores the nature of memory and of the soul, while the unfolding tale builds tension and anticipation like a whodunit” (Abraham Verghese). It has been named one of the New York Time‘s “Novels Everyone Will Be Talking About in 2026.” A mysterious accident along a country road sparks an awakening and an investigation in Akhtar’s most daring work yet—a visionary novel of spiritual transformation in an age of fracture. Akhtar’s work as a novelist and playwright has been published and performed in over two dozen languages. He is the winner of the Pulitzer Prize for Drama for his play Disgraced, which was also nominated for the Tony Award for Best Play. His other Broadway plays include McNeal, Junk, and The Who & The What. Akhtar is also the author of the novels American Dervish, a Kirkus Reviews Best Book of the Year, and Homeland Elegies, called “a tour de force” by The Washington Post. In 2021, he was named the New York State Author by the New York State Writers Institute, succeeding Colson Whitehead.

item.title: Inprint Hernan Diaz Reading
item.description:
Monday, October 12, 2026 at 7:30 PM

Location: Stude Concert Hall, Rice University, Entrance #18 & #20, 6100 Main St., Houston, TX, 77005, United States

General admission tickets will go on sale on Monday, September 21, 2026 at 12 pm. Season tickets are on sale here. Hernan Diaz will read from his new novel Ply, followed by an on-stage conversation led by a local author/journalist. The evening will conclude with a book sale and signing. The event is presented as part of the 2026/2027 Inprint Margarett Root Brown Reading Series.  Described by Lauren Groff as a “narrative genius,” Hernan Diaz is the Pulitzer Prize-winning and bestselling author of the novel Trust, named one of the New York Times’s Best 100 Books of the 21st Century and currently being developed as a limited series for HBO. His literary work is celebrated for its genre-bending reinvention of American mythology and its complex exploration of wealth, capitalism, and isolation. His first novel, In the Distance, was a finalist for the Pulitzer Prize and the PEN/Faulkner Award. His work has been translated into 37 languages. After rewriting America’s past in his two previous novels, from 1920s Wall Street to the 19th century western frontier, Diaz turns to the future with his new novel Ply. A combination of Dickensian odyssey, family drama, and scientific thriller, Ply examines the place of technology in the American imagination. Centuries from now, the state has been dismantled, and humans are reinventing social bonds and learning new ways to coexist with nature. Following a childhood defined by loss, survival, and found family, an orphan grows up to become a “pincher,” someone who steals electricity from the grid to sell it on the black market. “Diaz brilliantly envisions how love, trust, and loyalty can remain when freedom and justice have collapsed and makes every page exhilarating and meaningful” (Library Journal, starred review).

item.title: ESCRITORES EN LA CASA: Ezequiel Zaidenwerg
item.description:
Thursday, October 15, 2026 at 7 PM

Location: Inprint House, 1520 W Main St, Houston, TX, 77006, United States

Inprint recibe al autor argentino Ezequiel Zaidenwerg para presentar su nueva novela en verso, Fantasma escritor. Tras la presentación, Zaidenwerg conversará sobre su obra con un escritor local. Esta presentación forma parte de la serie de Inprint Escritores en la casa. Todas las presentaciones de Escritores en la casa son gratis y están abiertas al público.  Ezequiel Zaidenwerg nació en Buenos Aires en 1981. Es autor de varios libros incluyendo los poemarios Doxa (2007) y La lírica está muerta (2011, 2017). Además, es traductor de Mark Strand, Ben Lerner, Anne Carson, Weldon Kees, Robin Myers, Joseph Brodsky, Mary Ruefle, João Cabral de Melo Neto,  Brenda Hillman, Kay Ryan y Emily Dickinson, entre otros y otras. Es miembro fundador del colectivo de acción poética Como Un Lugar y envía diariamente por mail poemas traducidos a través de su newsletter El poema de hoy. Su primera novela, Fantasma Escritor, fue elogiada por Fernanda Trías, quien escribió: “Ezequiel Zaidenwerg dirige su inteligencia inquieta hacia los fantasmas que nos constituyen: la familia, la lengua, el duelo, el deseo, la herencia. Zaidenwerg, que con su newsletter El poema de hoy ha hecho de la poesía y la traducción una forma de encuentro colectivo, entrega ahora una primera novela íntima y luminosa, vulnerable y formalmente viva. Este es un libro sobre la traducción como una manera de estar en el mundo: el arte de escuchar aquello que nos rodea y de encontrar las palabras que acaso nos permitan decir yo.” Esta serie de lecturas es posible gracias a la Rita Mallett Blasser Foundation

item.description:

Free and open to the public Free copies of Anger Is Only a Shadow for the first 100 families Presentation and Q&A by the author Meet the author followed by a book sale and signing Appearance by celebrated Houston writer Jasminne Mendez Bus scholarships available for student groups – full scholarships for public schools, partial scholarships for private schools upon availability. For information, email info@inprint.org Books available through Kindred Stories And more! The 2026/2027 Inprint Cool Brains! Series proudly presents National Book Award winner and renowned poet Elizabeth Acevedo, sharing her new YA novel Anger Is Only a Shadow. Known for YA novels filled with poetry, humor, and heart, Elizabeth Acevedo is the New York Times-bestselling author of The Poet X, which won the National Book Award for Young People’s Literature, the Michael L. Printz Award, the Pura Belpré Award, the Carnegie medal, the Boston Globe–Horn Book Award, and the Walter Award. She is also the author of With the Fire on High, which was named a best book of the year by the New York Public Library, NPR, Publishers Weekly, and School Library Journal; and Clap When You Land, which was a Boston Globe–Horn Book Honor book and a Kirkus finalist. Acevedo is a National Poetry Slam Champion and served as the 2022 Young People’s Poet Laureate. “An irresistible story of family connection, resilience, and loyalty” (Kirkus starred review), Anger Is Only a Shadow is Acevedo’s powerful new YA novel in prose and poetry. Lil is anything but small. She’s rebellious, she’s loyal; she’s figuring out what kind of good person she wants to be, or if she wants to be a good person at all. But more than anything? Lil wants to be free. When her instinct for freedom leads to another stay in D.C. juvenile detention, Lil knows she’s lucky to just be on probation. But judgment, guilt, and an ankle monitor weigh heavily on her, and she can’t shake that pinned-down feeling. The only person who might understand is her big brother, Aldwin. Except he’s more distant now than just the hundred miles from his college. As her court hearing ticks closer, a question looms over Lil as the missed phone calls and strange texts from her brother pile up: will she stay put, or put her future freedom on the line? “A striking and nuanced portrait of the realities of juvenile detention and mental illness” (Publisher’s Weekly starred review) and “intensely genuine” (The Bulletin of the Center for Children’s Books starred review), Anger Is Only a Shadow is a white-knuckle journal to self-understanding and doing the right thing, no matter the cost.

item.title: Inprint Colson Whitehead Reading
item.description:
Thursday, November 12, 2026 at 7:30 PM

Location: Congregation Emanu El, 1500 Sunset Boulevard, Houston, TX, 77005

General admission tickets for $35, which will include a copy of Colson Whitehead’s Cool Machine, and will go on sale on Tuesday, October 13, 2026 at 12 pm. Season tickets are on sale here. Colson Whitehead will read from his new novel Cool Machine, followed by an on-stage conversation with a local author/journalist. The evening will conclude with a book sale and signing. The event is presented as part of the 2026/2027 Inprint Margarett Root Brown Reading Series.  Two-time Pulitzer Prize and National Book Award winner and #1 New York Times bestselling author Colson Whitehead comes to Houston with his new novel Cool Machine, the magnificent and highly anticipated final volume of his Harlem Trilogy that brings to life 1980s New York. In a starred review, Publishers Weekly writes, “Whitehead concludes his Harlem Trilogy with a transcendent and wildly entertaining novel in which his recurring characters grapple with the ways their lives are defined by crime and the city they call home. . . . The heists, stakeouts, and showdowns are rendered with grit and precision, but the real wallops come in breathtaking riffs on the city’s magnetic force. . . . It’s the greatest New York novel in years.” Whitehead is the first writer to win the Pulitzer for consecutive books: the historical novels The Underground Railroad (2016) and The Nickel Boys (2019). The Underground Railroad also won the National Book Award and was named one of the Ten Best Books of the Year by The New York Times Book Review. Known for innovative novels that explore social themes, while often incorporating fantastical elements, he is also the author of The Intuitionist, John Henry Days, and Sag Harbor, as well as The Colossus of New York, a book of essays about the city, and The Noble Hustle, a nonfiction account about the 2011 World Series of Poker. Among his honors, Whitehead has received MacArthur and Guggenheim Fellowships, a Whiting Writers Award, the Library of Congress Prize for American Fiction, and the National Humanities Medal. From 2018-2020, he served as the New York State Author.
